name: Curio
about: Curio is developing NuCycle, a used nuclear fuel recycling production facility, and in May 2026 asked the NRC to open a 10 CFR Part 70 docket for pre-application work toward an operating license. Engineering design is underway with Sargent & Lundy; the site had not been chosen as of May 2026.
expected_reason: Unclear: recycled fuel competes at the margin with enriched fuel; no incumbent in the map recycles at commercial scale.

verdict.what_it_builds: NuCycle, a used nuclear fuel recycling production facility. Curio asked the NRC in May 2026 to open a 10 CFR Part 70 docket for pre-application work toward an operating license. Engineering design is underway with Sargent & Lundy, and no site had been chosen as of May 2026.
verdict.buyers: The description does not name who pays for recycled fuel or recycling services. Likely reactor operators or fuel users, but this is unconfirmed.
verdict.reasoning: Curio is building a used nuclear fuel recycling facility, which the nuclear fuel lane covers but for which the map lists no operator. The listed companies work on enrichment, fuel fabrication and reactors, and none runs reprocessing, so the map cannot say whether this space is open. The filing shows early engineering work with Sargent & Lundy and no site yet, and the description gives no buyers, technology choice or funding. Call is look: worth a founder meeting to test demand and the licensing path.
open_questions: Which buyers would pay for NuCycle's output or service, and do any have signed offtake or letters of intent?
What separation technology does NuCycle use, and how far along is it beyond engineering design?
What is the planned site, and what is the timeline from the Part 70 pre-application to a license application?
How is the work funded, and how much capital is needed to reach a first operating facility?
Does Curio's team include the chemical separations and licensing staff needed to run a regulated fuel facility?

calls.why: The advanced nuclear licensing cost-share could cover part of the NRC pre-application and Part 70 work, but the listing gives no eligibility or scope detail, so the founders should confirm with DOE that a used fuel recycling applicant qualifies.
